name: rtk
tagline: Rust binary that compresses shell command output via PreToolUse hook. Rewrites about 100 supported commands (git, cargo, npm, find, grep, pytest) before output enters the agent context.
compactDesc: Shell output compression via PreToolUse hook
observations: Vendor reports 60–90% on CLI output (cargo test 91.8%, git status 80.8%, find 78.3%, grep 49.5%).
Third-party measurement (Patterson, Apr 2026): 1.33B tokens saved over 26,779 commands across one month on a single developer's production setup.
Documented silent-failure modes: PATH leak (issue #685), wrong-package collision, hook chain collision, cost regression #582.
Mitigations exist via a wrapper script. Hook PATH and stdout-to-pipe behavior need explicit handling.

name: lean-ctx
tagline: Single Rust binary covering shell compression and MCP-based code retrieval together. 49+ MCP tools plus 90+ shell patterns. Tree-sitter signature extraction across 18 languages.
compactDesc: Shell + MCP retrieval in one binary
observations: Vendor reports 60–95% compression and up to 99% on cached re-reads (per-call metric).
No independent third-party measurement found.
Changelog documents production failure modes: 50 GB BM25 index on monorepos, daemon stale-binary mismatches, fork-bomb hook recursion (fixed Apr 2026).
License migrated from MIT to Apache-2.0 mid-project.
Shell-hook side overlaps directly with rtk. Co-installation is not supported.

name: Headroom
tagline: Transparent API proxy that compresses request payloads between agent and provider. SmartCrusher (JSON), CodeCompressor (AST-aware), Kompress-base (ModernBERT). CacheAligner preserves Anthropic prefix-cache eligibility.
observations: Vendor benchmarks reproducible via pytest: SQuAD v2 97% accuracy at 19% compression, BFCL 97% at 32%, GSM8K zero delta.
Patterson (Apr 2026): 189M tokens saved on top of rtk with 96% prefix-cache hit rate on real Claude Code traffic.
Bundles the rtk binary in installation. Designed to compose with rtk rather than replace it.
Proxy-based integration is the primary deployment path; MCP-tool and SDK modes also exist.
Single primary maintainer. Paid macOS desktop variant (closed-source) provides commercial sustainability signal.

name: Context Mode
tagline: Plugin + MCP server that sandboxes large tool outputs (Playwright snapshots, gh issue lists, logs) into local FTS5 SQLite storage, returns summaries. SQLite event capture for session continuity.
compactDesc: MCP tool output sandbox + session memory
observations: Vendor numbers on tool-output sandboxing: Playwright snapshot 56 KB → 299 B, gh issue list 59 KB → 1.1 KB, access log 45 KB → 155 B.
Overlaps with Headroom MCP tools and proxy compression.
License recently changed from Elastic 2.0 to MIT.
Strongest fit for teams with significant Playwright or browser-automation workloads.

name: token-optimizer-mcp
tagline: MCP server with 61 specialized tools for caching, compression, and analytics. Brotli compression of MCP tool outputs in external SQLite, plus ARIMA/LSTM predictive cache and PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks.
observations: Vendor claims 95%+ reduction across 38K "operations". Per-tool numbers ("88% reduction", "91% reduction") are uniform across 60+ tools, which suggests synthetic measurements.
Tool-bloat paradox: 61 registered MCP tools consume context-window real estate via tool definitions. Net effect on <200K context windows unclear.
Latest release November 2025; no releases in ~6 months as of May 2026.
Repo shows characteristic AI-generated-codebase signals: high single-author commit count, semantic-release pipelines, auto-installing hook scripts.

name: Serena
tagline: MCP server providing symbol-level code intelligence via per-language Language Servers. Exposes find_symbol, find_referencing_symbols, replace_symbol_body, insert_after_symbol, rename, plus a project memory store.
observations: ManoMano Tech benchmark (Feb 2026, 36k LOC Java): described as "must-have" on multi-file refactors. 4x cost increase and 60% slower than vanilla agent grep on trivial read-only lookups.
Cold-start LSP warmup on large repos can take 10–60 seconds on the first query of a session.
Commercial sustainability via paid JetBrains plugin; OSS core stays free.
Installation via uvx adds uv and per-language LSPs to the provisioning surface.
Maintainers explicitly discourage plugin-marketplace installs.

name: CodeGraph
tagline: Local SQLite-backed call graph built from tree-sitter. Pre-indexed at init, instant queries thereafter. 19 supported languages, PHP not included.
compactDesc: Static call graph via tree-sitter + SQLite
observations: Vendor headline (README, May 2026): 94% fewer tool calls and 77% faster exploration across 6 benchmark codebases including the Swift compiler at 25,874 files with zero file reads.
Per-codebase numbers in the README range from 93–96% fewer calls and 43–82% faster, depending on language and size.
No independent third-party reproduction.
Mechanism is mechanically credible: pre-indexed call graph collapses grep fan-out into single MCP tool calls.
Star count grew from ~1.2k to ~4.6k between March and May 2026, driven by community marketing posts.
better-sqlite3 native dep requires Xcode CLT on macOS; WASM fallback documented as 5–10x slower.
Upstream of tokensave (the Rust port).
Single-author project despite the rapid star growth. Bus factor is unchanged by adoption rate.

name: Context+
tagline: MCP server combining RAG, Tree-sitter AST, Spectral Clustering, and Obsidian-style linking. Turns a codebase into a hierarchical feature graph with semantic clustering. Requires Ollama for embeddings and chat models.

meta.License: Not verified at time of cataloguing

observations: Vendor claim: "99% accuracy". No published benchmark methodology found.
Distinguishing mechanism: spectral clustering on file embeddings groups semantically related files into labelled clusters.
Requires running Ollama locally as the embedding and chat provider, which adds a separate model-management surface to the install.
OLLAMA_API_KEY is required in config even though Ollama is typically run locally without auth, which is unusual.
License not explicitly visible from search results; verify before any commercial use.
Distribution via bunx requires Bun runtime, distinct from npm/uvx-based competitors in the catalogue.

name: GitNexus
tagline: CLI + MCP server that indexes a repo into a property graph (LadybugDB, formerly KuzuDB) via Tree-sitter AST. Tracks call chains, dependencies, inheritance, execution flow. Optional in-browser embeddings. Auto-generates AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md.

meta.License: OSS + commercial license required for commercial use
meta.Agents: Claude · Cursor · Codex · Cline · Roo · Windsurf

observations: Star count grew from ~10k (March 2026, Paperclipped article) to ~28k+ (April 2026, MarkTechPost). Substantial community adoption signal.
License is dual: OSS for personal use, commercial license required for commercial use. Material consideration for consultancies and any non-personal deployment.
Backed by a commercial entity (akonlabs.com) offering managed SaaS and self-hosted enterprise options.
Deeper Claude Code integration than most: MCP tools, four agent skills (Exploring, Debugging, Impact Analysis, Refactoring), PreToolUse + PostToolUse hooks, auto-generated AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md.
Distinguishing mechanism: precomputed property graph at index time, not embedding-similarity retrieval. Designed for structural queries ("what depends on this?") rather than semantic ones.
Optional Leiden community detection generates per-module SKILL.md files under .claude/skills/generated/.
45 GitHub contributors per MarkTechPost article, but commit-graph concentration on single primary author keeps it classified as solo by our methodology. Vendor-affiliated alternative.
Browser-only mode runs entirely client-side via WebAssembly (Tree-sitter WASM, LadybugDB WASM, transformers.js embeddings). No data leaves the browser in that mode.

name: code-review-graph
tagline: Tree-sitter pre-built structural map of a repository written to SQLite. Parses functions, classes, imports, call relationships, inheritance, and test dependencies. Framed for code review and blast-radius analysis.
observations: Surfaced by the Milvus context-management roundup (May 2026).
Same mechanical category as CodeGraph (tree-sitter → SQLite) but framed for review/blast-radius.
Answers structural questions rather than semantic ones. Complementary to vector-search retrieval.
Maturity, language coverage, and community signal all need separate verification before any pilot.

name: tokensave
tagline: Rust port of CodeGraph. Single binary, native PreToolUse hook in Rust, libSQL + FTS5 + vectors. 15 languages including native PHP and Ruby via tree-sitter. Idempotent installer and built-in diagnostics.
compactDesc: Rust port of CodeGraph with native PHP
observations: No vendor or third-party measurement of token reduction available.
Two optional network calls: anonymous token-count upload to a Cloudflare Worker, and a GitHub version check. Upload defaults on.
Inherits architectural choices from upstream CodeGraph (also single-maintainer).
Native PHP support without external LSP is notable for Drupal-heavy stacks.
Star count and contributor count are the lowest in this survey.

name: Claude Context
tagline: MCP server doing hybrid BM25 + dense-vector code search via Milvus. Requires Zilliz Cloud or local Milvus plus an embedding API provider.
observations: Augment Code internal benchmark reports ~40% token reduction at equivalent retrieval quality.
External-service requirement introduces a recurring spend line separate from the coding-agent bill.
Client codebases under NDA require explicit sign-off before being embedded by third-party providers.
Strongest fit for semantic ("find authentication logic") queries that don't map to specific symbols.
Recommended by its own vendor in the May 2026 Milvus roundup. Vendor affiliation noted.

name: MCP Language Server
tagline: Thin LSP-over-MCP wrapper exposing raw primitives: definition, references, rename, diagnostics, code lens. No memory layer, no project context, no symbolic editing abstractions.
compactDesc: Raw LSP primitives exposed over MCP
observations: Functionally a subset of Serena, using the same LSP foundation without higher-level operations.
Smaller surface area, simpler dependency tree.
No published benchmarks or independent measurements.

name: Semble
tagline: Local code search via static Model2Vec embeddings (potion-code-16M) + BM25 fused via RRF, with code-aware reranking. CPU-only, no transformers at runtime, no API keys, no GPU, no Milvus. Drop-in MCP for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode.
compactDesc: Local vector search via 16M static model
observations: Vendor benchmark: 0.854 NDCG@10 across 1,250 query/doc pairs over 63 repos in 19 languages, vs 0.862 for CodeRankEmbed Hybrid (137M-param transformer). 99% of best transformer quality at ~218x faster indexing and ~11x faster queries.
Vendor claims 98% fewer tokens than grep+read. No independent reproduction yet (project launched on Hacker News May 2026).
Removes the cost+NDA deal-breaker that affects Claude Context (no embedding API, no Milvus, no cloud). Stack runs entirely on the developer's machine.
MinishLab also maintains Model2Vec (the underlying embedding library) and ships potion-code-16M on HuggingFace, providing organizational backing beyond a single repo.
Distribution via uvx adds uv to the provisioning surface; same dependency footprint as Serena. No native deps beyond standard scientific Python.

name: Token Savior
tagline: MCP server for progressive code reading. Returns summary → snippet → full file on demand instead of dumping whole files into context by default.
observations: Surfaced by the Milvus context-management roundup (May 2026).
Three-layer pattern (summary → snippet → full file) mirrors how developers actually navigate code.
Conceptually overlaps with Serena's symbol queries; differentiated by progressive-expansion API.
Maturity, language coverage, and community signal need separate verification.

name: Caveman
tagline: Claude Code skill plus plugin and rule files for other agents. Instructional only: directs the model to drop articles, hedging, and pleasantries, with intensity levels (lite, full, ultra, wenyan).
observations: Vendor benchmark: 65% output reduction (range 22–87%) vs "answer concisely" baseline.
Guzik (Apr 2026) replication on Sonnet and Opus: 14–21% real-world output savings.
Pillitteri field test (PHP and Python, one week): 15–25% reduction with quality preserved on mechanical tasks, degraded on architectural discussion and onboarding.
Output tokens are the smaller share of coding-session cost; net session impact correspondingly smaller than the headline.
`ultra` mode produces telegraphic output that may not suit client-facing PR descriptions or code review.

name: claude-token-optimizer
tagline: Bash init.sh that scaffolds a documentation layout (CLAUDE.md, .claudeignore, .claude/ tree). Framework-specific examples for Express/Next/Vue/Nuxt/Angular/Django/Rails/NestJS/Laravel.
observations: Vendor claims 90% reduction (11K → 1.3K tokens) measured on the author's own bloated repo. Result depends on pre-existing doc bloat.
curl | bash install pattern from a 5-star, single-maintainer repo.
Pure file-system scaffolding. Works with anything that reads CLAUDE.md + .claudeignore.
No package, no plugin, no MCP. No releases yet; 12 commits.

name: claude-token-efficient
tagline: Single CLAUDE.md file (plus three optional profiles: coding, agents, analysis) containing roughly 12 rules banning sycophantic openers/closings, em-dashes, prompt restatement, "As an AI..." framing, scope creep.
observations: Vendor 63% claim from a 5-prompt directional test; README admits "not a statistically controlled study" with "no variance controls."
File itself adds persistent input-token overhead on every turn, which can flip net savings negative on short queries.
Issue #1 (2026-04-01): shorter 7–12-line configs outperform the full rule set.
Co-author "claude" suggests file is Claude-generated. Low supply-chain risk (Markdown only).

name: memsearch
tagline: Markdown-first cross-session memory. Decisions stored as human-readable .md files; Milvus used as a rebuildable retrieval index. Progressive recall (search → expand → drill to transcript).
observations: Surfaced by the Milvus context-management roundup (May 2026); same vendor.
Markdown-first storage means the memory artefact is human-editable, version-controllable, and survives loss of the vector index.
Cross-session, cross-agent, cross-model memory positioning.
Milvus dependency adds operational burden similar to Claude Context.
No independent third-party measurement.

name: ClaudeMem
tagline: Persistent cross-session memory store for Claude Code. Vendor claim: 10x token savings on session startup by avoiding re-loading project context.
observations: Project has an associated Solana token ($CMEM), unrelated to the OSS code but distinct from typical OSS tool brand profiles.
Anthropic's native compaction beta plus disciplined CLAUDE.md usage cover much of the same ground.
No independent third-party measurement found.

name: token-optimizer
tagline: Pure-stdlib telemetry plugin that reads Claude Code session JSONL files, scores session quality (S–F), profiles per-turn cost, detects anti-patterns, audits CLAUDE.md and MEMORY.md health.
observations: Passive observer: reads session JSONL, produces dashboards. No interception of the prompt chain.
v5 added bash output compression for 16 commands; overlaps with rtk if both run (disable via TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_BASH_COMPRESS=0).
An audit layer is the only way to make any other tool's savings measurable across a fleet rather than anecdotal.
